editorial: If you like old-school ghost stories, this one pulls you in fast. Arthur Kipps is a young lawyer sent to a lonely village to sort papers in a dead client’s house. The place feels cold and quiet, and the locals clearly know more than they say. As Arthur works alone, he starts seeing a woman in black and learns a sad, scary secret tied to the town. The movie builds tension slowly, using shadows, sounds, and long hallways instead of loud jump scares. Daniel Radcliffe gives a serious, grounded performance, and the setting does a lot of the heavy lifting. The story is simple, but it keeps you watching because every clue feels important. It is not packed with action, so viewers wanting nonstop thrills may find it slow. Still, if you enjoy creepy houses, mystery, and a dark mood, it is a strong pick. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.

At first it seems to work, but the Woman in Black is not done. At the train station, Arthur sees her, and his son Joseph walks toward the tracks. Arthur jumps to save him, but both are killed by a train. The ending reveals they are reunited with Arthur’s late wife, while the ghost remains watching.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves gothic ghost stories and slow-burn scares.
